Use Muse Spark 1.3 max and the full available token budget. Work from PR #94 final behavior commit 7dc1277999778155e13819c97a7543aa3966d7e2, stacked on the green tire work. Hard evidence already established: M5 300-ft skidpad 0.986 g; strict validation 0 FAIL; tire pure-slip post-peak retention ~90% at 15 deg and ~80% at 20 deg; combined slip, AWD torque split, load sensitivity, track asphalt mapping, camber/contact signs and rear-steer phase are not currently proven defects. Mobile wheel is now 900 deg lock-to-lock default and ordinary 60 deg hand input stays below 8 deg peak front slip from 30-100 km/h. Do not raise peak mu, weaken B=15, add analog speed caps, or retune a coefficient just to improve a subjective number. Diagnose actual normal-path behavior, quantify before/after, and only propose a small behavioral patch when evidence beats the current branch. Any behavior change must include deterministic regression coverage and preserve test:tire, test:cornering, test:conventions, test:tire-feel, test:m5-validation:strict, track QA and build as applicable.

Lane 3 — formal double-lag A/B study. Build a deterministic matrix: stock both lags; slip-only; force-only; neither; plus one physically motivated candidate. Compare 30/50/70/100 km/h step steer and 60/90deg hand-wheel cases using yaw onset, 10-90 rise, front slip, lateral G, overshoot, force energy sanity and strict M5 validation. Rank candidates and recommend exactly one architecture, not a parameter grab-bag.
